key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, welding speed, and current affect molten pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability in distinct ways.
engineering_relevance: These trends can guide parameter selection for Invar welds used in aerospace composite molds, balancing penetration, weld width, and arc stability.
method: Numerical simulation of molten pool dynamics
Comparison across laser power, welding speed, and current
evidence_signal: Within the studied ranges, higher laser power (5–6 kW) increased penetration and arc deflection tendency, higher speed (0.5–0.8 m/min) reduced penetration and width, and higher current (150–170 A) widened the weld and improved arc stability.
watch_item: The abstract reports parameter-specific trends but no quantitative validation errors or mechanical-property results, limiting conclusions about predictive accuracy and final joint performance.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
